1.w: The burden that Habakkuk the prophet saw.

2.w: Until when, O YHWH, will I cry out, and you will not hear? I cry out to You, “Violence!” And will you not save?

3.w: Why do you cause me to me see iniquity and to look upon trouble? Destruction and violence [are] before me, and there is strife, and contention rises up.

4.w: Over this, the law is numb, and justice does not go forth forever. For the wicked are surrounding the righteous. Upon thus, twisted justice goes forth.

5.w: “Look among the nations and observe them, and be utterly astonished. For a work [I am] doing in your⁺ days, [that] you⁺ would not believe even if it were recounted.

6.w: For behold, I am raising up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation, marching through the breadth of the earth, to possess dwelling places not unto them.

7.w: He [is] terrible and fearsome; his justice and his dignity go forth from him.

8.w: Their horses are swifter than leopards and fiercer than wolves of the evening; their horsemen spring about; and their horsemen come from afar, and they fly like the eagle hurrying to devour.

9.w: They all come for violence; the full force of their faces [is] the east wind, and they gather captives like the sand.

10.w: And he mocks the kings, and princes [are] an object of scorn for him; at every fortification he laughs, and heaps up earth and seizes it.

11.w: Then he sweeps through like the wind and passes on; he is guilty, this one; his power [is] unto his god.”

12.w: [Are] You not from everlasting, O YHWH my God, my Holy One? We will not die. O YHWH, for judgment You have appointed them, and, O Rock, for reproof You have established them.

13.w: Purer of eyes than to behold evil, and You are not able to look on wickedness. Why do You look on those acting treacherously, [and] remain quiet when the wicked is devouring one more righteous than he?

14.w: And You make mankind like the fish of the sea, like creeping things without one ruling over them.

15.w: He brings up each with a hook; he catches him in his net, and gathers him in his dragnet; upon thus he is glad and rejoices.

16.w: Upon thus he sacrifices to his net, and burns incense to his dragnet, because by them his portion [is] rich and his food fat.

17.w: Upon thus he will empty his net, and continue to slay nations without having mercy?
